content_layers.observation_text: Prehospital responders meet death at speed, thresholds, documents, panic, and uncertain authority; the archive must distinguish their witnessed burden from emergency instruction.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The sources support recognizing professional grief, compassion fatigue, moral distress or injury, cumulative exposure, debriefing, and role-specific burden as part of the deathwork ecology, while keeping worker accounts consent-bound and nonpublic by default.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: For DeathVocab, this is a worker-carried-death record: it preserves the fact that workers hold bedside and afterdeath knowledge in memory, body, craft, and burden, without demanding confession or turning suffering into content.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Render only after worker-support, workforce-privacy, role-specific, organizational-nonblame, fieldwork-extraction, and publication-language review. Do not publish identifiable patient, family, worker, employer, call, body, scene, or institution details.

what_this_is_not: a legal, emergency, forensic, funeral, benefits, staffing, or employment advice surface
a request for workers to confess trauma for the archive
uncertainties: Worker burden varies by role, setting, workload, institutional culture, exposure, community, and personal history.
Public sources do not replace consented worker testimony, supervisor review, occupational-health expertise, or local institutional policy.
Some worker accounts may be publishable only as composite paraphrase or not at all.
content_layers.lay_orientation: This record exists so the archive remembers that the people who know dying rooms also carry those deaths. It does not ask them to become material for readers.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Future fieldwork must ask about craft, vocabulary, and role boundaries before asking about painful memory; workers retain edit, withdrawal, and no-quote rights.
language_notes: Avoid hero/martyr framing, toughness tests, voyeuristic trauma language, and blame of individual workers.
Distinguish grief, burnout, compassion fatigue, moral distress, and moral injury without diagnosing anyone.
Name organizational context when sources support it, but do not accuse living institutions without evidence and review.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not include names, employer, dates, rare role/location combinations, patient or family details, call audio, body images, case descriptions, shift narratives, private messages, or quotes that could identify a worker, patient, family, facility, agency, or decedent.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record to diagnose or treat worker grief, burnout, compassion fatigue, moral injury, trauma, substance use, depression, anxiety, or occupational distress.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer staffing duties, labor rights, reporting duties, employment obligations, debriefing requirements, forensic duties, emergency duties, or funeral-service obligations from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not universalize how workers in different traditions, communities, professions, or institutions should process deaths.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical, mental-health, occupational-health, legal, emergency, forensic, funeral, staffing, management, or employment advice; qualified local support and institutional policies govern actual worker support.
safety_notes: Worker grief is part of the evidence ecology but not public property.
The archive should preserve craft knowledge without requiring workers to expose their wounds.
Do not use worker memories as proof against patients, families, institutions, or traditions without independent review and consent.
